Meta.title: AutoMergeNet: AutoML-Based M-Source Satellite Data Fusion Evaluated With Atmospheric Case Studies
Meta.venue: IEEE JOURNAL OF SELECTED TOPICS IN APPLIED EARTH OBSERVATIONS AND REMOTE SENSING

hypothesis_1.hypothesis: The authors hypothesise that their proposed framework, AutoMergeNet, which uses neural architecture search for satellite image data fusion, will outperform existing baseline methods on multimodal classification problems.
hypothesis_1.reason: The abstract states that existing approaches 'cannot be transferred to other related problems, as they rely on expert-selected features and manual pipeline design.' The paper then proposes AutoMergeNet as a general framework. The abstract concludes by stating the outcome of their evaluation: 'AutoMergeNet performs strongly and consistently on these two multimodal classification problems, outperforming six baseline methods'. This implies a hypothesis that their proposed method is superior to the baselines.

experiment_1.experiment_description: The performance of the proposed AutoMergeNet framework is evaluated against six baseline methods on two multimodal classification tasks: methane plume detection and carbon monoxide plume detection.
